title: Oracle-lint e auditor dividem MAX_REPLAN_ROUNDS=2: o linter faminta o auditor
description:
O BLOCK do oracle-lint deterministico e o BLOCK do auditor compartilham o mesmo orcamento MAX_REPLAN_ROUNDS=2 (plan-runner.ts:108, guard :1509 partindo de roundsCompleted=1 em :1507), ou seja 1 round inicial + no maximo 1 re-plan. Consequencia estrutural: todo PRD que tropeca no linter fica sem NENHUM round de correcao pos-auditor e escala direto.

Evidencia medida, plano do CAM-447 em 2026-07-28, event log .claude/cam-worker-events.jsonl:
- 01:06:56 planner spawn 1 (uuid ebbc3e3f)
- 01:16:19 planner spawn 2 (uuid d5fb3306), o round de re-plan
- 01:23:05 auditor spawn (uuid c06fd40c), UMA unica vez
- 01:27:51 plan-escalated, roundsCompleted=2

Nenhum auditor rodou entre os dois planners. O round 1 foi bloqueado por runOracleLintCheck (chamado em plan-runner.ts:1324, sintetiza um PlanVerdictReport BLOCK via buildLintBlockReport :962-978 ANTES do auditor ser spawnado) e consumiu o unico round de re-plan pelo mesmo canal buildReplanPlannerTaskPrompt (:123-139). O auditor entao rodou uma vez, devolveu 5 findings medidos e escalou na hora, com zero chance de correcao. Os findings eram bons e concretos: 1 critical (nenhum criterio carrega sweep red-on-main, e um oraculo de US-002 ja e verde em main hoje, logo verifica nada), 2 important (US-001 nao consegue satisfazer os proprios gates typecheck/test dentro do file set que declara; e um oraculo compara measuredAt por dia de calendario, insatisfazivel numa remedicao honesta no mesmo dia), 2 suggestion.

Agravante: o linter e conhecidamente over-firing (CAM-438). Um gate deterministico que erra esta consumindo o orcamento do auditor LLM que acerta.

Agravante 2, perda de trabalho: um fresh `cam plan` comeca CEGO. buildPlannerTaskPrompt (:1402, :77-83) recebe so o issue id; o marker .cam-plan-escalated.json e lido unicamente por status.ts:657 para display; e clearStalePlanArtifactsFn (:1380) deleta prd.json e plan-verdict-report.json no topo de todo run. Entao re-despachar o mesmo issue destroi os findings do auditor e o planner re-deriva do zero.

Consertar: orcar os rounds de lint e de auditor separadamente, ou nao contabilizar o BLOCK do linter contra o budget do auditor, de forma que todo PRD receba ao menos um round de correcao pos-auditor antes de escalar. Considerar tambem persistir os findings do ultimo audit para que um re-plan do mesmo issue nao comece cego.

Relacionado: CAM-438 (lint over-fire), CAM-442 (round de re-plan invisivel).

spec.scope: Stop the deterministic oracle-lint from consuming the AUDITOR's re-plan budget, so that a PRD which trips the lint still gets a post-auditor correction round before escalating. Measured shape of the defect: runOracleLintCheck (src/supervisor/plan-runner.ts:994-1004) returns Extract<PlanPhaseResult, { kind: 'audit-blocked' }>, byte-identical in kind to the auditor's own block at :1344, and runPlanPhaseWithReplan (:1500) counts both with ONE counter (roundsCompleted, :1507) against ONE guard (roundsCompleted < MAX_REPLAN_ROUNDS, :1509) with no predicate distinguishing origin. There is exactly one runtime read of MAX_REPLAN_ROUNDS in the whole repo (:1509). Measured consequence on the CAM-447 plan (event log, 2026-07-28): planner at 01:06:56 and 01:16:19, auditor spawned exactly ONCE at 01:23:05, plan-escalated at 01:27:51 roundsCompleted=2, discarding 5 auditor findings including 1 critical. IN SCOPE: an origin discriminator on the audit-blocked result; separate, independently-bounded counters for lint-origin and auditor-origin rounds; and recording WHICH budget was exhausted on the .cam-plan-escalated.json marker and the plan-escalated event, since once two budgets exist a bare roundsCompleted is ambiguous. DELIBERATELY NOT IN SCOPE: (a) the lint's precision, it over-fires and that is CAM-438; (b) persisting audit findings so a re-plan does not start blind, a different verification mode and fix surface; (c) re-plan round invisibility, CAM-442; (d) the fact that buildReplanPlannerTaskPrompt's text at :135 says 'BLOCKED by the auditor' verbatim even on a lint-origin block, which is a real but pre-existing prose defect to be filed separately. CRITICAL DESIGN CONSTRAINT, measured, do not get this backwards: when the lint blocks EVERY round the auditor should still never be spawned (ADR-0040: never spend the auditor on a provably-broken PRD). The invariant is NOT 'the auditor must always run'. It is narrower: LINT ROUNDS MUST NOT CONSUME THE AUDITOR'S CORRECTION BUDGET.
acceptanceCriteria: AC1 [species: change-DETECTING, swept RED against main 2026-07-28]. A lint-origin block must not spend the auditor's correction budget: when round 1 is blocked by the oracle-lint and the following round's AUDITOR returns BLOCK, the run must perform a further post-auditor correction round instead of escalating, because the auditor budget has been consumed only once. Add a test to test/supervisor/plan/plan-runner-replan.test.ts named EXACTLY 'lint round 1 leaves the auditor budget intact and a post-auditor correction round still runs', driving runPlanPhaseWithReplan via the existing options-builder harness with readPrdContentFn injected to return a lint-FAILING prd on round 1 and a lint-clean prd on every later round, verdicts ordered [APPROVE, BLOCK, APPROVE], asserting the terminal kind is 'audit-approved' and that the auditor was spawned at least twice. [oracle: out=$(bun test test/supervisor/plan/plan-runner-replan.test.ts -t 'lint round 1 leaves the auditor budget intact and a post-auditor correction round still runs' 2>&1); echo "$out" | grep -qE '[1-9][0-9]* pass' && echo "$out" | grep -qE ' 0 fail'] SWEEP RECORD: this exact form was run against main on 2026-07-28 and is RED (bun reports 'matched 0 tests'); the byte-identical form pointed at an existing test name is GREEN on main, so the redness is the missing behaviour, not a broken form. The nonzero-pass-count conjunct is MANDATORY and must never be reduced to a bare exit-code check, because a bun -t filter matching zero tests must not be able to satisfy this oracle.

AC2 [species: change-DETECTING, swept RED against main 2026-07-28]. The durable escalation marker and the plan-escalated event must each name which budget was exhausted. Add a discriminator to PlanEscalatedMarker (src/supervisor/plan-escalation.ts:37-43), thread it through PlanEscalationWriterParams (plan-runner.ts:1422) and the writeMarker call (:1533-1538), and add the same field to PlanEscalatedEventDetail (src/supervisor/events.ts:498-501) and the emitted detail (:1546-1552). Add a test named EXACTLY 'escalation marker and event name the exhausted budget'. [oracle: out=$(bun test test/supervisor/plan/plan-runner-replan.test.ts -t 'escalation marker and event name the exhausted budget' 2>&1); echo "$out" | grep -qE '[1-9][0-9]* pass' && echo "$out" | grep -qE ' 0 fail'] SWEEP RECORD: RED against main on 2026-07-28 by the same two-sided control as AC1.

AC3 [species: change-DETECTING, swept RED against main 2026-07-28]. Separating the counters must not introduce an unbounded planner spin: a run whose oracle-lint blocks on EVERY round must terminate as kind 'plan-escalated' with AC2's discriminator naming the oracle-lint budget, and total planner spawns across the call must stay bounded by the sum of the two budgets. Add a test named EXACTLY 'lint budget is independently bounded and escalates naming the oracle-lint budget'. [oracle: out=$(bun test test/supervisor/plan/plan-runner-replan.test.ts -t 'lint budget is independently bounded and escalates naming the oracle-lint budget' 2>&1); echo "$out" | grep -qE '[1-9][0-9]* pass' && echo "$out" | grep -qE ' 0 fail'] SWEEP RECORD: RED against main on 2026-07-28 by the same two-sided control as AC1.

AC4 [species: invariance PIN, measured GREEN on main 2026-07-28, must stay GREEN]. The pure-auditor path is behaviourally untouched: MAX_REPLAN_ROUNDS keeps its name and its value of 2 and remains the AUDITOR budget, so the existing spawn-cycle pin keeps passing unmodified. [oracle: out=$(bun test test/supervisor/plan/plan-runner-replan.test.ts -t 'escalation: exactly MAX_REPLAN_ROUNDS planner\+auditor spawn cycles occur \(no 3rd round\)' 2>&1); echo "$out" | grep -qE '[1-9][0-9]* pass' && echo "$out" | grep -qE ' 0 fail'] This is the joint-satisfiability guard on AC1: a fix that merely raises or re-points MAX_REPLAN_ROUNDS would satisfy AC1 while breaking this, and that pairing must be caught before dispatch. Three separate tests assert the constant equals 2 (test/supervisor/plan/plan-replan.test.ts:99-101, test/plan-runner-in-progress-conflict.test.ts:211, and this pin), so introduce the lint budget as a NEW exported constant rather than renaming or re-scoping this one.

AC5 [species: invariance PIN, measured GREEN on main 2026-07-28, must stay GREEN]. When the lint blocks EVERY round the auditor must still never be spawned, per ADR-0040. This is the constraint most likely to be inverted by a careless reading of this issue, so it is pinned explicitly against the existing test. [oracle: out=$(bun test test/supervisor/plan-runner.test.ts -t 'AC4: exhausting re-plan rounds on a persistently-broken oracle escalates via writeEscalationMarkerFn, auditor never spawned' 2>&1); echo "$out" | grep -qE '[1-9][0-9]* pass' && echo "$out" | grep -qE ' 0 fail']

AC6 [species: change-DETECTING]. The one test that codifies the CAM-447 pathology as expected behaviour must be REWRITTEN to assert the new contract, never deleted: test/supervisor/plan-runner.test.ts:425, named 'mixed: round-1 lint-block then round-2 real auditor BLOCK both fold into the SAME escalation path', currently asserts that exactly this scenario escalates with roundsCompleted 2. Under AC1 that scenario must no longer escalate. Its replacement must keep a test whose name still begins with 'mixed: round-1 lint-block then round-2 real auditor BLOCK' and must assert the non-escalating outcome. [oracle: out=$(bun test test/supervisor/plan-runner.test.ts -t 'mixed: round-1 lint-block then round-2 real auditor BLOCK' 2>&1); echo "$out" | grep -qE '[1-9][0-9]* pass' && echo "$out" | grep -qE ' 0 fail'] Requiring a surviving test under that name prefix is what stops the contradiction being resolved by deletion, which would otherwise turn this oracle vacuous.

AC7 [species: invariance PIN]. Backward compatibility of the persisted marker: a .cam-plan-escalated.json written by an older binary, lacking AC2's new field, must still parse rather than being rejected by the shape guard at src/supervisor/plan-escalation.ts:66-81, which today validates exactly five fields. The new field must therefore be optional at the read boundary even though it is always written. Cover it with a test in test/supervisor/plan/plan-escalation.test.ts asserting a five-field marker still round-trips.

AC8 [species: invariance PIN, comparand derived live, no frozen integer]. The quality spine stays green: bun run typecheck exits 0 and bun test reports zero failures. Deliberately expressed as a zero-failure assertion and NOT as a pass-count floor or equality, because a pinned pass count rots on every added test, which is exactly the defect recorded as CAM-447. [oracle: bun run typecheck && out=$(bun test 2>&1); echo "$out" | grep -qE ' 0 fail'] SWEEP RECORD: GREEN on main 2026-07-28, typecheck 0 errors and 5750 pass / 0 fail.
AC9 [species: invariance PIN]. The lint spine stays green. [oracle: bun run check:all]
gotchas: Do not invert the core constraint. Lint-blocks-every-round SHOULD escalate without ever spawning the auditor (ADR-0040). The defect is only that a lint round CHARGES the auditor's budget. AC5 pins the correct half so a fix cannot 'solve' AC1 by making the auditor always run.

runOracleLintCheck early-returns null when readPrdContentFn === undefined (plan-runner.ts:998). Every existing test in plan-runner-replan.test.ts leaves readPrdContentFn unset, which is exactly why none of them currently touch the lint path. A new test that forgets to inject it will silently drive the auditor path and pass for the wrong reason. The only file that currently injects it is test/supervisor/plan-runner.test.ts.

The options-builder harness in plan-runner-replan.test.ts advances the per-round verdict via roundIndex++ inside teardownPlanPanesFn (around :195-203), not inside the runner. Any test overriding teardownPlanPanesFn must preserve that side effect or every round reads verdict[0] forever and the test passes or hangs for the wrong reason.

test/supervisor/plan/plan-runner-replan.test.ts:328-333 asserts the marker payload with toEqual on exactly {issueId, summary, findings, roundsCompleted}. Adding AC2's field breaks it by construction; update that assertion rather than working around it. Same for the round-trip toEqual assertions in test/supervisor/plan/plan-escalation.test.ts:35 and :106.

test/unit/status-projection.test.ts:68-72 and test/unit/status-diagnostics.test.ts:81,:227,:409-413 construct PlanEscalatedMarker literals; they break if AC2's field is required at the type level for readers. AC7 is what keeps this tractable.

The enforcement point for AC1 is the POST-loop branch at plan-runner.ts:1531, not only the loop guard at :1509: after the loop exits, escalating requires that the relevant budget actually be exhausted. Changing only the guard leaves the terminal wrong.

bun's -t filter is a regex, so a test name containing + or parentheses must be escaped (see AC4's form). A -t filter matching zero tests is reported by bun as an error but must never be treated as oracle success, which is why every oracle here demands a nonzero pass count.

Worst-case planner spawns per plan call rise from MAX_REPLAN_ROUNDS to lint-budget + auditor-budget. That higher ceiling is the intended correct behaviour, not a regression, and AC3 is what keeps it finite.
This issue does not fix CAM-438 (lint over-fire). A perfectly precise lint would still be wrong to charge the auditor's budget, so CAM-448 stands alone and must not absorb CAM-438.
